papers.title_in_file: Quantum Semi-Random Forests for Qubit-Efficient Recommender Systems
papers.version_note: arXiv:2508.00027v1 [quant-ph], 30 Jul 2025. The text layer is damaged in places: equations 1 to 3 lost their summation signs, Algorithm 1 is flattened, the sentence about sparsity on the ICM matrix is garbled (the percent sign and a clause are lost), Key Takeaway 3 ends at 'using 90', and a flat exponent such as 10-3 stands for ten to the minus three. The paper uses the names QsRF and QsRL for the same model, and says 'three-stage' in the abstract while describing four stages (Stage 1 to Stage 4).
papers.what_it_is: A short arXiv preprint that compresses item tags with a 1000-atom learned dictionary, selects 5 atoms with a depth-3 QAOA run on the PennyLane simulator, and scores recommendations with a bagged-tree ensemble on the QuantumCLEF ICM-150 and ICM-500 benchmarks.

assertions.value: The authors state that they present a three-stage hybrid machine learning algorithm that compresses tag profiles, optimizes feature selection under a fixed qubit budget via QAOA, and scores recommendations with a Quantum semi-Random Forest built on just five qubits.

assertions.value: The authors state that the QAOA step requires exactly five qubits and that their dense 20×20 QUBO matrix fits comfortably on five logical qubits.
assertions.anchor: Section I-B, p.2; Section II-C(a), p.3
quotes: then conduct feature selection with a depth-3 QAOA that requires exactly five qubits
yields a dense 20×20 QUBO matrix Q = − diag(w) + µ 11⊤ that fits comfortably on five logical qubits
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' claim; the paper gives no circuit encoding that maps 20 binary variables onto five qubits.
assertions.reader_inference: The mask z has one binary variable per candidate atom (20 of them) and the cost Hamiltonian is a sum of Z_i Z_j terms over the same indices as Q, which is the standard one-qubit-per-variable encoding and needs 20 qubits. The paper shows no encoding that reduces this to five. The headline 'five qubits' figure is therefore unsupported as written; this bears directly on the title claim.

assertions.value: The authors define a binary mask over the candidate set of Ktop = 20 atoms with a budget of k = 5, an energy with a penalty weight of about ten cubed that enforces selecting exactly k atoms, and a dense 20×20 matrix Q equal to − diag(w) + µ 11⊤.
assertions.anchor: Section II-B and II-C(a), Eq. (3), p.3

Let z ∈ {0, 1}Ktop be a binary mask over T and k = 5 the desired budget.
yields a dense 20×20 QUBO matrix Q = − diag(w) + µ 11⊤
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines the QUBO in Section II-C(a).
assertions.reader_inference: As written, Eq. (3) is a linear term plus a penalty that depends only on the number of selected atoms, so its minimum is the top-k atoms by weight w_j, which a sort finds classically; the QAOA step then has nothing to add. This is also the paper's own fallback rule. Algorithm 1 states a different Q (see algorithm1-qubo-differs).
